statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 4 because CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00Z Friday and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon; Stress is 41, moderate, as reciprocal 50% US-Canada tariffs now in force, a Canadian dollar-for-dollar response of unstated scope, a recall of nearly three million Tesla vehicles in China, crude up about 5% for a second week and a long end near multi-decade highs all sit unpriced until the Sunday reopen.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion: cash NDX halted a five-day slump, reclaimed its 29,142.44 low up to 29,405.12, closed below its own open at 29,308.86 and left VIX at 14.89 near the session low, while the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. The venue has been shut since 21:00Z Friday and reopens on Sunday at 22:00Z, about ten hours beyond the end of this horizon, so the published Tail describes the absence of a tradable price path rather than a view on direction. Stress stays inside the moderate band and drifts modestly higher across the weekend as North American tariff escalation, a large single-name recall, an elevated energy complex and a heavy long end accumulate with no venue able to price them. No danger window is published because no trading session falls inside the horizon.
headline: Closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across all twenty-four published hours while in-force 50% US-Canada tariffs, a promised Canadian counter-tariff and a near-three-million-vehicle Tesla recall accumulate as unpriced weekend risk, and Tail holds the closed-venue floor of 4.
body: CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run from 2026-08-22T12:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T11:00:00Z and end about ten hours before the reopen. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and the August expiry cleared without one-way structure; reporting frames the session as halting a five-day slump on stronger US activity data, with crypto-linked equities leading as bitcoin gained about 22% on the week. One widely used quote source read materially away from that print during this run and self-labelled its data as delayed, so the level was corroborated against an independent quote page and two session wrap reports before use. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00% and near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. H.15 for 20 August shows the 2-year at 4.19%, the 5-year at 4.39%, the 10-year at 4.69% and the 30-year at 5.23%, the long end having reached its highest in nearly two decades earlier in the week. WTI is quoted near $87.06 and Brent near $94.39, each up roughly 5% for a second consecutive week, with Strait of Hormuz throughput still depressed and Iran-Oman routing talks unresolved. Since the halt, the United States imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian goods at 12:01 a.m. ET, Ottawa suspended negotiations and committed to matching them dollar for dollar without itemising scope, and Tesla disclosed a recall of just under three million vehicles in China over emergency door releases, effective 25 September, after TSLA closed 5.14% higher. None of this can be priced by any equity venue inside this horizon. Tail therefore holds a flat closed-venue floor of 4 in every slot and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON, while Stress opens at 41, troughs at 38 through the thinnest weekend window and caps at 44 inside the moderate band as the unpriced stack lengthens. Next week's calendar is dense but sits entirely beyond this horizon: July PCE and the second Q2 GDP estimate on Wednesday morning, Nvidia after the Wednesday close, and the Jackson Hole symposium with the Fed Chair keynote on Friday.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is close to complete: 22 hourly assessments are available and the 05:00Z and 06:00Z clock-hours on 22 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout. The path is coherent with the session that produced it: 14 through the European afternoon of 21 August, a drift to 16 into the 14:00Z US cash-open window with a brief event/whipsaw mode around the August expiry, a return to the low teens through the afternoon, a step down to 10 at 20:00Z and then to 5 and 4 once the 21:00Z halt removed price discovery. Stress fell in parallel from a 58 peak at the open to 35-38 overnight as realised volatility decayed and VIX closed near its session low, then edged back to 40 as the tariff and recall headlines landed. Confidence stayed in the 84-88 band throughout, and no hour in the window carried a Tail reading anywhere near the block threshold.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the final slot begins at 2026-08-23T11:00:00Z and ends about ten hours before the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds a flat closed-venue floor of 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON in every slot. Stress opens at 41, eases to a 38 trough through the quiet Saturday evening window when weekend news flow is thinnest, then drifts to a 44 cap by the final slots as in-force North American tariffs, an unquantified Canadian counter-tariff, a near-three-million-vehicle Tesla recall, crude up about 5% for a second week and a long end near multi-decade highs accumulate without a venue able to price them; it stays inside the moderate band throughout. Confidence opens at 87 on a well-verified but settled evidence set and decays gradually to 80 in the final slots as the last tradable print recedes to roughly thirty-seven hours old, remaining in the high band across the whole horizon. Any repricing of the weekend stack would first present as a Sunday-evening opening gap outside this horizon, to be scored against live evidence by a later cycle.
